steps.text: Stir brown sugar, melted butter, and cinnamon together in a small bowl; spread into the prepared pan. Spread apple pie filling evenly over top, then layer on bread slices, pressing down as you go.
Beat milk, eggs, and vanilla together in a bowl; slowly pour over bread, making sure egg mixture is completely absorbed. Cover pan with aluminum foil; refrigerate 8 hours to overnight.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Bake in the preheated oven, covered, for 1 to 1 ¼ hours. Turn on the broiler. Uncover pan; drizzle maple syrup on top. Broil until syrup begins to caramelize, 2 minutes. Remove from oven; let stand for 10 minutes, then cut into squares. Invert pan onto a serving tray or baking sheet so apple filling is on top. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Overnight Apple Cinnamon French Toast
raw_recipe.description: Overnight apple cinnamon French toast, made with apple pie filling, cinnamon, and white bread, is a great brunch recipe — perfect for large gatherings.

review.reviewBody: I have made this recipe a couple of times and everyone has loved it!!! A couple of things I noticed is that I could only fit about 9 slices of bread in the pan before it started overflowing and it took 1 1/2 hours for mine to cook. I think next time I make it I will only use one can of apple pie filling and then I will be able to add more bread. Also make sure you spray the foil or it will stick.

I have made this a fewtimes and everyone just loves it! Instead of the canned pie filling, I used fresh apples (3-6), peeled and thinly sliced. I tossed those with 1/2 cup melted butter (3/4 cup leaves a soppy, greasy mess at the bottom), 3/4 cup brown sugar, and 2-3 teaspoons cinnamon. I have always been able to fit eighteen slices of bread in my 9x13 pans (three layers of six). This bakes up perfectly in 70-75 minutes. Spraying the tin foil is an absolute MUST or it will stick. This recipe will be around our house for a long, long time. It's absolutely perfect!

I will definitely be making this again!!! The first time that I made this I followed the directions to a 'T' but the down fall was that using slices of bread invited people to take a full slice instead of scooping out a portion so that everyone could enjoy. This time I used brioche bread cut up in cubes. I still ran out because this dish is so delicious!!!!

I read the reviews followed tips that other reviews gave and it turned out awesome! I used an 11x17 pan without changing the ingredient amounts. I used evaporated milk instead of regular milk and baked it for about 90minutes before drizzling the maple syrup on & broiling it. I put a bit of melted butter to coat the pan and then added about a tsp of lemon juice and a sprinkle of ground nutmeg, ground cloves and cinnamon to the 2 cans of apple pie filling (to avoid it being overly sweet) before spreading it in the pan. I found a local bakery makes french toast bread which is thicker sliced white bread with maple syrup baked in (yum!), and I used the entire loaf which was 20 slices. A few of the slices I cut in half to fill the pan and I really smooshed the bread down into the apple pie filling. After pouring the egg mixture (to which I also added spices) onto the bread, I used a rubber spatula to spread the egg mixture all over the bread filling in any extra spaces. It turned out firm and not soggy with wonderful apple flavor to compliment the traditional french toast flavor. I would make it over again just the same. Everyone loved it, and the few slices I had leftover tasted kind of like an apple fritter or streudel pastry when I had a slice cold from the fridge the next morning. A good to go breakfast! It never needed any additional butter or syrup on top even when it was warm from the oven. I'm so glad I read the reviews and made the adjustments I did! Recipe reviews can be

This recipe looked really fantastic to me--easy to make, ideal for a busy morning b/c you do everything the night before but cook it, and I love apples so that addition to French toast was right up my alley. When I prepared this, I thought two cans of apples seemed like a lot but one didn't exactly cover the pan so I used two. I used Pepperidge Farm cinnamon bread and that was a great addition. It wasn't 20 slices but whatever was in a loaf completely filled my glass 9x13 to the brim (two layers of bread). Too bad I didn't account for the expanding bread when it baked and I ended up with a mess in my oven because the juices bubbled up and over. Be sure to use a taller 9x13 if you can, or put a baking sheet under to catch the overflow. It still baked through and looked great. Unfortunately, it was way too sweet, and I'm a big fan of sugar, my friends. So for me to think it's so sweet it was almost inedible is something. Because I loved the cinnamon/apple combo, I'll give this another whirl but will use thinly sliced fresh apples. The brown sugar/butter in the bottom of the pan will be plenty to sweeten those up to what I hope will be an ideal level.

Everyone loved it! Did not use as much bread and only one can of pie filling. Cooked it at least 1 1/2-1:45 hours. Instead of syrup, I sprinkled with cinnamon and sugar and then broiled top. Turned it out upside down so apples ended up on top. Served with all kinds of berries and fruit on the side. Definitely making this again for my breakfast crowds!

I was glad to see that other reviewers had used fresh apples rather than pie filling. I knew I would not like the pie filling. So, I substituted Honeycrisp apples for the filling and used Aldi marbled cinnamon bread. Fabulous! No worry about oven spill over or middle sogginess. I did take the foil off for the last 10 minutes per other reviews.

This is easy and delicious! Like others, I thinly sliced fresh apples and lightly sautéed them in a little bit of butter instead of using canned pie filling - they were perfect! I also used whole wheat bread (16 slices, fitting 8 to my pan and then adding a second layer of bread). I increased the eggs from 6 to 8 so that each serving had the equivalent of one whole egg. I baked it for 75 minutes to make sure it wasn't soggy. Adding real maple syrup and broiling for two minutes was a nice touch - really finished it off!

I have always been able to fit eighteen slices of bread in my 9x13 pans (three layers of six). This bakes up perfectly in 70-75 minutes. Spraying the tin foil is an absolute MUST or it will stick. This recipe will be around our house for a long, long time. It's absolutely perfect!

I made 2 glass pans (9 x 13) last night using 1 french loaf in each pan cut in large cubes. I used unpeeled cored sliced apples with honey and butter with a sprinkle of cinnamon for the bottom of one pan and the other I did the same to the apples except I added dried cranberries. yummmy...In the egg mixture, I put eggs, 1/2 & 1/2 cream, vanilla, cinnamon and 1 tbsp of sugar.I put bread cubes in a bowl a little at a time and poured the egg mixture over it then put it loosely on top of the apple mixture then sprinkled a tsp of sugar on the top. This morning, the family and son's friend thought it was chronic (awesome)! ;) I will definitely make this again because it is prepared all the night before then in the morning you only have to pop it in the oven!

This makes way to much for just the two of us. What I have tried that is easy to make the number of servings you need. Aldi stores have apple strudel bread (at least they do in the fall). I mekd the french toast by dipping the bread in a milk and egg mixture with afew teaspoons of sugar and cinnamon to taste. Let the bread soak this up a bit. Fry in a bit of butter. Tastes great topped with maple syrup or powdered sugar. Or try browing apple slices in butter then add brown sugar, apple cider and cinnamon. Simmer for awhile to thicken sauce. The apple mixture is also good on pumpkin spice pancakes
I make this for Christmas morning! I usually use brioche bread instead of plain white bread. If I can find cinnamon brioche even better!
Delicious and easy. Sweet enough without syrup. Will make again. Thanks
Everyone liked it, the only problem was the 20 slices of bread, I only got 12 slices in the pan. That seemed great plenty.
Made this for Christmas brunch. Everyone loved it. Used cinnamon raisin bread less brown sugar and added roasted pecan pieces after removing it from the oven.

Made this with fresh apples and it was delicious. I am wondering if anyone has tried freezing it before baking and then thawing in the fridge before baking. Not sure how far in advance I can make it Thursday to eat on Sunday seems a bit far in advance without freezing.

Everyone loved it! I used 7 eggs because I increased the milk to 2 cups instead of 1.5 cups. I also added another tsp of vanilla. Be very careful when broiling the syrup on top- don’t walk away from the stove- 1 or 2 minutes is all that’s necessary when the casserole is on the top shelf of the oven! I also sprinkled some more brown sugar on top of the casserole before covering it back up to cook. It’s delicious - other fruit fillings could also be used! This will become a staple around my house!
I have been making over and over. It is delicious. I use less sugar and substitute the maple syrup with less honey.

I don’t normally cook so easy is always good. Fifteen minutes prep the night before, marinate, then put in oven and bake. I will make this again but will not turn over. I will use a deeper baking dish since I only used half the amount of bread. 

I also complemented with baked omelette casserole.
